heroHeadline: AP Investigation: ICE Detainee Suicides at Unprecedented Rate — 10+ Deaths Since Trump's Return; Delaney Hall Hunger Strike Day 5 Erupts in Clashes; Venturella Takes Over June 1
heroSubtitle: An Associated Press investigation published May 27, 2026 found that ICE detainee suicides have reached an unprecedented pace in the agency's two-decade history: at least 10 suicides since Trump's January 2025 inauguration, with 7 since October 2025 alone — already more than any full fiscal year on record. Nine of ten who died were Hispanic men; average age 32; most had been in custody less than a month. At least three facilities failed to provide mental health screenings within ICE's required 12-hour window. Simultaneously, a five-day hunger and labor strike by 300+ detainees at the GEO Group-operated Delaney Hall facility in Newark, NJ, escalated into street clashes on May 26 as masked ICE agents wielded batons against protesters outside the facility — prompting DHS to call demonstrators 'rioters.' The 287(g) local enforcement program reached a new record of 1,870 Memorandums of Agreement as of May 26, up 172% since January 2025. Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons departs May 31; former GEO Group executive David Venturella takes over June 1 as the first ICE director drawn from the private detention industry. The Senate returns this week for a floor vote on the $71.7B ICE/CBP reconciliation package.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, California AG, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, Congressional records, Roll Call, CBS News, NPR, NBC News, CNN, AP, CalMatters, Washington Post, Boston Globe, Punchbowl News, KFF, Murthy Law Firm, Time Magazine, and Vermont Public
